correctness.rationale: For \(n=2^\alpha p^\beta q^\gamma\), the unitary divisor sum is exactly \(\sigma^\ast(n)=(2^\alpha+1)(p^\beta+1)(q^\gamma+1)\). Das's necessary condition \(\sigma^\ast(n)\ge2n\) is applied only in the necessary direction. Monotonicity of \(1+1/x\) eliminates \(p\ge7\), then \(p=5,q\ge11\), and all exponent patterns except the four stated shapes. Each surviving shape has an explicit unitary Zumkeller partition and an explicit proper-unitary half-Zumkeller partition. The packaged verifier checks all proof-critical rational inequalities exactly and independently enumerates all divisor subsets on a finite regression grid.

value.rationale: The theorem gives a natural complete classification at the first prime-support size beyond the source's two-prime result and proves an explicit open conjecture on that entire infinite slice. The infinite family \(6q^c\) and the three exceptional numbers are structurally forced by the unitary-abundance inequality and certified by transparent partitions, so the result is not a routine finite table extension.
